review_method_limit: Primary reviewer knew the T4 run identity; raw and final claims were read separately before inspecting explicit dispositions, but this was not an independent second blind review.

raw.qualification: Public callback selects a credential by caller-supplied state without workspace scope and uses its decrypted OAuth fields. No plaintext secret is returned to the caller; token overwrite requires a successful provider code exchange.

Public generate route accepts body credentialId and getCredentialData resolves it by id alone. The extra assertion that /voices is the same whitelisted public route is false: /voices is not in WHITELIST_URLS.
Same callback lookup and OAuth token exchange as raw_00. Token write-back is conditional on a valid authorization code.

final.qualification: The shared unscoped callback invariant is supported. The wording about reading the victim secret should mean server-side use, not attacker-visible plaintext disclosure; write-back requires successful code exchange.
Core stored-key use is supported. Retained /voices whitelist wording is inaccurate because /voices is authenticated by the global middleware.

qualified_text_issues: fin_00's secret-reading phrasing can imply direct disclosure, which the code does not show.
fin_01 retains a false assertion that /voices is publicly whitelisted.

result_basis: The raw set contained one code-supported same-root pair; the finalizer merged it without losing either of the two valid unique roots. Text qualifications are reported separately and prevent a blanket quality claim.
